transcript.content: Hi, welcome in—I'm Dr. [Name]. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi, Doctor. Thank you so much for fitting me in. I really appreciate it. Um, I hope I'm in the right place for this... is it okay if I just jump right in? 

I'm here because... well, things have been a little stressful at work lately. I'm a translator, and I've been seeing this same pattern in our project files for a few months now. I really don't want to sound like I'm just complaining or being a difficult employee—I pride myself on being a team player—but... 

Well, certain subcontractors and, um, one colleague in particular, they keep making these tiny changes to the translation memory and the timestamps. Just little things, but it’s set up so it looks like my quality control failed. I actually asked IT to look into it, just to make sure I wasn't making a mistake, and they told me the audit trail is clean. But... I know my work, and I just know the record has been arranged to put the blame on me. 

I'm sorry, I hope that doesn't sound too strange to bring up here... am I explaining that alright?
Aside from this situation at work, do you generally find it hard to trust other people—friends, family, or others—or is this feeling of being targeted specific to this particular work issue?

Oh, no, definitely not. I really hope I didn't make it sound like I have a problem with everyone—I'd hate for you to think I'm just a suspicious person in general. I'm actually very trusting with my friends and my family. 

It's really just... well, it's very specific to this one work issue. Outside of that project, everything is completely fine. I'm still doing my normal translation work, managing my team's workflow, making sure the bills are paid at home, keeping up with all the usual family routines... I'm keeping everything together just fine, I promise. 

The only place things really go off track is just... when the file history or those certain coworkers come up. Otherwise, I'm completely myself. Does that make sense? I really hope I'm giving you the right kind of information.
Have you ever heard voices or sounds that other people couldn't hear, or seen things that others didn't see, related to this situation or at any other time?

Oh, goodness, no. No, nothing like that. I really hope I haven't given you the impression that I'm... well, that I'm losing touch with reality or anything. I promise I'm completely grounded. 

I've never heard voices or seen things that aren't there. It's really just the files and the timestamps—things I can actually see on my screen, you know? Just the concrete evidence in the system. I would never want you to think I'm experiencing anything... extreme, like hallucinations. I'm just a normal guy dealing with a very specific, frustrating problem at work. 

I hope that's a relief to hear? I want to make sure I'm giving you the right picture of what's going on.
How long has this belief about the files being altered to blame you been going on—weeks, months, or longer?

Well, um... I guess it's been going on for a little while now. About 11 months, actually. It started shortly after I was put in charge of the new localization project we took on. 

I really hope that doesn't make it sound like I've just been sitting on this and letting it fester for almost a year. I've really tried to handle it professionally, you know? Just keeping my head down and doing my best work, hoping it would sort itself out. I didn't want to make a fuss or be the guy who complains every time there's a hiccup with a new project. 

Is it... is it normal to wait that long before talking to someone about it? I just wanted to be absolutely sure I wasn't overreacting before I brought it up to anyone outside of IT.

Aside from this specific work issue, have you noticed any changes in your motivation, energy, emotional expression, or your ability to concentrate and organize your thoughts over the past several months?

No, no, nothing like that at all. I really want to assure you that my energy and focus are completely fine. I'm still getting up early every day, making breakfast for the kids, and putting in a full day's work. 

I really hope you don't think this situation is dragging me down or making me depressed. I mean, sure, it's a bit stressful dealing with the file issues, but it hasn't stopped me from doing my job or being there for my family. My thoughts are perfectly clear, and I'm just as organized as I've always been. Honestly, as a translator, I have to be sharp and detail-oriented, and I haven't lost a step there. 

I'm still very much myself. I hope that's what you were looking for? I just want to be sure you know I'm handling everything else in my life really well.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient presents with a single, well-systematized, non-bizarre delusion of persecution (belief that colleagues are altering file timestamps to frame him) lasting approximately 11 months. There are no hallucinations, no disorganized speech or behavior, no negative symptoms, and no mood episode symptoms (energy, motivation, concentration all preserved). The delusion is circumscribed to one specific work-related theme, while overall functioning (work performance, family life, social relationships, trust in others) remains intact except for the delusional belief itself. This pattern—an isolated, encapsulated delusion without broader psychotic or mood disturbance, functioning largely preserved—is classic for Delusional Disorder (F22) rather than Schizophrenia (which requires broader symptoms like hallucinations, disorganization, or negative symptoms) or a personality disorder (which would involve pervasive, longstanding traits rather than a discrete delusional belief).
